canonical_data: Agent definitions, typed tool implementations, prompts, session state, and MCP server configuration
current_repo_note: AWS renamed the canonical repository from strands-agents/sdk-python to strands-agents/harness-sdk; the published packages remain strands-agents.
strengths: Model-driven design keeps agent definitions short while leaving tools, prompts, and model choice explicit
Publishes Python and TypeScript packages plus its own MCP server, so the same agent definition reaches several runtimes
Backed by AWS with documented multi-agent patterns and a separate maintained tools repository
weaknesses: The canonical repository was renamed, so older integration guides and third-party references point at a stale path
Persistence, permissions, and production recovery remain application-defined rather than framework-guaranteed
A large open-issue count relative to the project's age indicates a fast-moving surface
why_it_matters: Gives the Atlas a provider-published, model-driven agent SDK whose design deliberately minimizes framework scaffolding, contrasting with graph-and-workflow frameworks.
